samples.line: - **ADR-003 (open tension, not a decision):** Serving practice has converged on evicting window-local KV and recovering it by *bounded approximate recompute* rather than persisting it (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 2026, §3.2.2 — replay `w_in` tokens instead of `L × w_in`, with the truncation trained for). This is directly in tension with ADR-002: bounded replay produces exactly the state the drift guards exist to reject. Adopting it requires a typed residency class for which equivalence is explicitly not claimed, so the guards keep full force everywhere else — a tolerance dial on the existing guards would void them globally and is refused. Not adopted; recorded so the tension is visible before anyone reaches for it under KV pressure. R-217 owns the decision.

samples.after: - **ADR-004:** Where a storage format omits a scaling level, the omission is admissible only against a *declared magnitude bound*, not against measurement alone. Worked instance (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 2026, §2.4.4): E2M1 with one E4M3 scale per 16 channels, dropping NVFP4's second-level global scale, justified by deriving the bound from model structure — RMSNorm weight magnitude ≈ 1, so a 512-channel normalised latent has L2 norm ≲ √512 ≈ 22.6; RoPE preserves norm, so the post-rotation per-channel maximum is bounded likewise; observed training maximum ≈ 10 against a format maximum of 2688. A bound derived from structure is checkable at admission; "it worked in our tests" is not.
samples.before: - **ADR-002:** Exo-Flash doctrine: online-softmax kernels avoid materializing S/P matrices; FA1/FA2/FA3 papers (Dao et al. 2022; Dao 2024; Shah et al. 2024) fully describe the algorithm, licensing in-house implementation.

samples.line: - **ADR-003:** A dtype used for *residency* is chosen against different constraints than one used for *arithmetic*, and the catalogue must not imply they are interchangeable. A cache dtype may be dequantised immediately before compute, which deliberately removes any requirement for native matmul support in that format — that is what keeps an aggressive storage format portable across hardware that cannot multiply in it. The dtype vocabulary already covers this (`Mxfp4`, `F4E2M1`, packed dtypes carrying group size + scale layout); what is absent is a dispatch-side field naming the storage dtype, so a request can declare all six compute stages and remain ambiguous about the bytes it reads. R-220 owns the profile change; the precision-profile concept page owns the argument.
